issue.title: Refine Design system colors and type scale layout
issue.description:
Refine the Design system preview so Colors and Type scale sit side-by-side as flat padded sections rather than bordered cards, while reorganizing Colors to mirror the sidebar token grouping and turning Typography into a true descending type-scale specimen.

Overall layout

* Keep the Design system tab read-only and live.
* At wider widths, place Colors and Type scale side-by-side in one shared layout.
* Remove the individual card borders/surfaces around both sections.
* They should feel like flat sections contained in ordinary divs with comfortable padding, not nested cards.
* Use spacing/alignment to separate the two sections rather than card chrome.
* At narrower widths, stack the two sections cleanly.

1. Colors section

Grouping/order:

* Mirror the semantic token grouping and order used in the Workbench sidebar.
* Do not keep the current broader Design-system-only groups if they differ from sidebar organization.
* Preserve side-by-side pairing for related background/foreground tokens.

Examples of pairings to preserve where applicable:

* Background / Foreground
* Primary / Primary foreground
* Secondary / Secondary foreground
* Accent / Accent foreground
* Card / Card foreground
* Popover / Popover foreground
* Destructive / Destructive foreground
* Sidebar / Sidebar foreground
* Sidebar primary / Sidebar primary foreground
* Sidebar accent / Sidebar accent foreground

Other singleton tokens such as Border / Input / Ring / chart tokens should follow the same sidebar grouping/order without inventing new presentation aliases.

Color item styling:

* Keep swatch + semantic token name + resolved value.
* Make swatches slightly larger than the current Design system preview.
* Change resolved token values from Mono typography to Sans/Body typography.
* Keep token names readable and compact.
* Keep the section visually denser/narrower than the current implementation so Type scale can sit beside it comfortably.

Sidebar token behavior:

* Continue showing effective Sidebar colors.
* When dedicated Sidebar tokens are OFF, reflect accepted base aliases.
* When dedicated Sidebar tokens are ON, reflect dedicated values.

2. Rename Typography to Type scale

Rename the existing Typography section heading to:
Type scale

Remove semantic-role groupings such as:

* Heading
* Body
* Muted
* Mono

The purpose of this section is now to show font-size progression rather than typography-role categories.

3. Type scale rows

Render one straight vertical list from largest to smallest.

Recommended order:

* text-5xl
* text-4xl
* text-3xl
* text-2xl
* text-xl
* text-lg
* text-base
* text-sm
* text-xs

If source inspection shows the accepted project supports a slightly different practical subset, keep the same descending largest-to-smallest principle.

Each row should contain:

* small muted utility label on the left showing the Tailwind class name;
* specimen text on the right rendered at that actual text size.

Use a consistent sample sentence such as:
"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."

Typography behavior:

* Use the live current Body/Sans family for the specimen rows so the size progression is easy to compare.
* Keep the active theme's relevant font family/weight/tracking behavior live.
* Do not create separate Heading/Body/Mono specimen groups in this section.
* The class labels themselves should remain small and secondary.

4. Flat-section treatment

For both Colors and Type scale:

* remove individual card borders;
* remove nested card-style background treatment unless the parent preview surface already provides the needed background;
* keep comfortable padding;
* preserve clear section headings;
* do not add shadows solely to separate sections;
* avoid nested-dashboard/card visual language.

Design intent:

* The Design system tab should feel like one clean reference sheet.
* Colors and Type scale should both be visible at once on wide layouts.
* The section should be easier to scan and less vertically long than the current version.

Live linkage / boundaries

* Preserve live updates from sidebar theme edits.
* Preserve light/dark behavior.
* Preserve Theme v3, history, persistence, import/export, Design Command, and mutation behavior.
* Do not duplicate editing controls.
* Do not create a second theme state.
* Do not add new public resources or tokens.

Accessibility / responsiveness

* Preserve top-level tab keyboard/focus behavior.
* Ensure token names/values and type-scale labels remain readable in light/dark.
* Reflow cleanly at narrow widths.
* Avoid horizontal overflow from large type specimens; wrap or constrain specimen text cleanly while preserving the visible size progression.

Acceptance

* Colors and Type scale appear side-by-side at suitable wider widths.
* They stack cleanly at narrower widths.
* Neither section is rendered as an individual bordered card.
* Both retain comfortable internal padding.
* Colors grouping/order mirrors the sidebar token organization.
* Related foreground/background tokens remain paired side-by-side.
* Color swatches are slightly larger than before.
* Token values use Sans/Body instead of Mono.
* Typography section is renamed to Type scale.
* Heading/Body/Muted/Mono grouping is removed from Type scale.
* Type scale runs from largest at the top to smallest at the bottom.
* Rows show Tailwind size labels on the left and live-sized specimen text on the right.
* Live theme edits continue to update both sections immediately.
* No responsive, accessibility, persistence, history, or Design Command regression.
